Mills_tail_proof: For x>=6,1<=x/6. Thus Q(6)<=integral_6^infinity x*phi(x)/6 dx=phi(6)/6<exp(-18)/15. Every omitted positive term of exp(18) is nonnegative, so the rational Horner polynomial is a lower bound and its reciprocal supplies an upper bound.
normalized_truncation_proof: Write q=Q(6). On[-6,6],F_T(x)=(F(x)-q)/(1-2q). Its difference from F is q*(2F-1)/(1-2q); because F lies in[q,1-q], its magnitude is at most q. Outside[-6,6] it is also at most q. This is a one-sided-tail bound, not the two-sided2q mass.
midpoint_CDF_proof: Binning conditional mass into uniform-x midpoints makes its discrete CDF at any x equal the conditional CDF at an adjacent bin edge at distance at most h/2. The density is at most phi(0)/(1-2q), so the discrepancy is at most phi(0)*h/[2*(1-2q)], including left/right limits at the atoms. Triangle inequality and q<=q_upper then yield the saved KS upper.
coordinate_BV_transfer: For a bounded-variation scalar observable, Stieltjes/step-function integration bounds an expectation difference by TV(f)*KS. The original positive GBM coefficients make each coordinate payoff increase on a single survival half-line and then drop to zero. Each discounted payoff lies in[0,40], so variation is at most80. This bound is uniform in every other continuous or discrete driver. Replacing independent scalar laws one at a time gives80*d*KS.
clipping_to_40_reason: Both ideal original and alternative laws use the same strict monitored barrier and already-discounted payoff in[0,40]. Their absolute expectation difference is also at most40.
